boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented CSUSM rituals and recurring events, from a Luiseño-named welcome and Cougar Coin Challenge to spirit chants, ceremonial maces and midyear commencement.

cards.title: Begin the Year With “Hello”
cards.subtitle: A Luiseño-named night of Cougar traditions
cards.notes: Wear Cougar Blue to Forum Plaza and join the chants and fight-song practice; students under 18 should arrange the required waiver early.
cards.short_summary: Miiyu turns the Luiseño word for “hello” into CSUSM’s spirited welcome for a new academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM’s 2025 event page identifies Miiyu as a new-year kickoff where students learn spirit chants and the fight song while wearing Cougar Blue.
cards.access_notes: The documented 2025 event ran at Forum Plaza from 8–11 p.m.; students under 18 needed a signed guardian waiver arranged through New Student and Family Programs.

cards.title: Accept the Cougar Coin Challenge
cards.subtitle: A ceremonial task inside new-student convocation
cards.notes: Listen for instructions during New Student and Family Convocation; the coin challenge is built into the formal welcome rather than a drop-in activity.
cards.short_summary: A named coin challenge gives CSUSM’s new-student convocation its own ceremonial twist.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM’s 2025 Weeks of Welcome listing says New Student and Family Convocation participants take part in the ceremonial Cougar Coin Challenge.
cards.access_notes: The documented 2025 convocation was held inside The Sports Center in separate morning and midday sessions; confirm the current invitation before attending.

cards.entity_name: Leave Your Mark Incoming Class Photo
cards.title: Fit an Entire Class Into One Frame
cards.subtitle: The annual incoming-student photo at Leave Your Mark
cards.notes: Arrive before the announced photo time and follow staff placement directions; the documented version welcomed both first-year and transfer students.
cards.short_summary: Leave Your Mark gathers CSUSM’s newest Cougars for an annual class portrait with a distinctly paw-themed wardrobe.
cards.evidence_claim: An official CSUSM account describes Leave Your Mark as a Weeks of Welcome signature event featuring the annual incoming-class photo.
cards.source_title: Semester Kicks Off with Packed Social Calendar
cards.access_notes: The cited photo and shirt details document the 2016 edition; consult the current Weeks of Welcome schedule before planning to participate.

cards.title: Learn the Fight Song at Miiyu
cards.subtitle: A 2016 original that now anchors the welcome chants
cards.notes: Use Miiyu’s guided practice to learn the current words and cadence instead of relying on an old recording or unofficial transcription.
cards.short_summary: CSUSM unveiled its first official fight song in 2016 and now teaches it during the Miiyu welcome.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM documented the unveiling of its first official fight song in 2016, and the 2025 Miiyu listing says students learn the fight song there.
cards.source_title: Semester Kicks Off with Packed Social Calendar
cards.access_notes: Fight-song instruction was included in the documented 2025 Miiyu program; verify the current Weeks of Welcome schedule for the next session.

cards.title: Spell the Mascot From the Stands
cards.subtitle: “C-C-COU, G-G-GAR” with the BLU CRU
cards.notes: Join only when the student section leads the call, then answer with “COUGARS”; attend a current home game to see whether the chant remains in rotation.
cards.short_summary: The BLU CRU’s split-spelling cheer turns the word “Cougar” into a CSUSM game-day call and response.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM’s NewsCenter printed the “C-C-COU, G-G-GAR” chant and described BLU CRU’s grassroots student movement as a tradition at athletic events.
cards.access_notes: The chant is documented in a 2015 university feature; game admission and current BLU CRU participation vary by event.

cards.title: Start Basketball Season With Fog and Dunks
cards.subtitle: CSUSM’s own spin on Midnight Madness
cards.notes: Watch for the fall Athletics announcement, then expect team introductions, student games, cheer and dance performances, and a closing dunk contest.
cards.short_summary: Cougar Madness introduces CSUSM teams and signals the opening of basketball season with a campus-specific arena show.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM reports that Cougar Madness began in 2016, returned in 2024 after a five-year hiatus and marks the start of college basketball season.
cards.source_title: Basketball Teams Kick Off Season in Style at Cougar Madness
cards.access_notes: The cited return was held at The Sports Center on Oct. 10, 2024; check Athletics for a future date and any admission requirements.

cards.title: Process to Mangrum in Cap and Gown
cards.subtitle: The documented commencement walk along the athletic fields
cards.notes: Treat this as a historical CSUSM commencement practice: the cited march occurred in 2011, and present ceremonies may use a different route or venue.
cards.short_summary: Graduates once followed Pomp and Circumstance along the athletic fields toward Mangrum Track and Field.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM’s account of its 2011 commencement names the “March to Mangrum” and describes graduates processing to Mangrum Track and Field as guests cheered.
cards.source_title: Celebrating on Campus: Class of 2011 Welcomes Graduation Ceremonies Back to Campus
cards.access_notes: Historical practice documented at the 2011 on-campus commencement; it should not be assumed to be part of the current ceremony route.

cards.title: Recess Behind a Luiseño-Carved Mace
cards.subtitle: A commencement object tied to the tukwut mascot
cards.notes: Look for the two official maces during commencement recessional; the informal wooden mace is the one connected to CSUSM’s tukwut relationship.
cards.short_summary: One of CSUSM’s official ceremonial maces is a Luiseño-carved wooden object honoring the campus mascot relationship.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM documented student and faculty marshals carrying two official maces in the 2011 recessional, including a wooden mace carved by a Luiseño tribal member.
cards.source_title: Celebrating on Campus: Class of 2011 Welcomes Graduation Ceremonies Back to Campus
cards.access_notes: The mace’s role is documented in the 2011 recessional; current display or procession arrangements should be confirmed with Commencement.

cards.title: Graduate at the Academic Year’s Midpoint
cards.subtitle: A December ceremony created for fall finishers
cards.notes: December graduates should follow Commencement instructions for the assigned college ceremony; the event moved to Frontwave Arena in its third year.
cards.short_summary: CSUSM gives December graduates a dedicated midpoint ceremony rather than making them wait until spring.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM reports that its third annual fall commencement served 1,040 graduates and that the ceremony debuted in 2023 for students finishing in December.
cards.source_title: More Than 1,000 Graduate as Fall Commencement Moves to New Venue
cards.access_notes: The cited third annual ceremony was held at Frontwave Arena in Oceanside; participation and guest access follow current Commencement rules.

cards.title: Launch a Rocket on Super STEM Saturday
cards.subtitle: The campus’s annual all-ages science festival
cards.notes: Check the current activity list, then plan a hands-on route through rockets, chemistry and astronomy demonstrations; younger visitors are welcome.
cards.short_summary: CSUSM’s recurring science festival turns campus demonstrations into an all-ages day of experiments and discovery.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSM’s official 2024 announcement identifies Super STEM Saturday as an annual event with more than 75 hands-on activities for attendees of all ages.
cards.source_title: Science to Engage Thousands at Annual Super STEM Saturday
cards.access_notes: The cited 2024 festival was free, open to the public and held from 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; verify the next event date before traveling.
